newsitem.title: USA: Dow Corning Q1 sales growth hurt by strong dollar.
newsitem.headline: Dow Corning Q1 sales growth hurt by strong dollar.

text.p: Dow Corning Corp said Wednesday that sales volume in the first quarter continued to grow at rates comparable to the previous two quarters, but the rising value of the dollar reduced reported sales growth by about three percent.

The company, a joint venture of Dow Chemical Co and Corning Inc, reported first quarter net income of $53.4 million, up from $51.9 million a year earlier. Revenues rose 2.5 percent, to $632.7 million from $617.2 million.

The maker of silicon-based products said volume growth rose in Japan and Europe, except for Germany. Americas and Pacific Rim growth continued at rates similar to the previous several quarters, it said.
Operating profitability was helped by cost containment efforts. After-tax earnings benefited from higher interest income and a lower net tax rate, it said.
"Management of expense growth relative to revenue growth ...has been and will continue to be critical to our future success," said John Churchfield, chief financial officer.
Dow Corning is operating under Chapter 11 protection because of thousands of lawsuits that allege the company's silicon-gel-filled breast implants caused health problems.
